senses.definition: to report or represent in outline
senses.example: The memo adumbrates the main features of the new policy.

senses.definition: to indicate faintly; to foreshadow
senses.example: Early skirmishes adumbrated the coming war.

senses.definition: to combine or unite to form one organization or structure
senses.example: The two schools amalgamated last year.

senses.definition: not likely to provoke dissent or offense; inoffensive, often deliberately so
senses.example: The official statement was anodyne and said nothing new.

senses.definition: a painkilling drug or medicine
senses.example: The doctor gave him an anodyne for the pain.

senses.definition: to inform or tell someone
senses.example: The nurse apprised the family of the patient's condition.

senses.definition: to stop or check progress or a process
senses.example: Early treatment can arrest the spread of the disease.

senses.definition: to attract someone's attention
senses.example: An odd sight arrested her attention on the way home.

words.note: Beyond detaining a suspect, arrest means to stop a process.

senses.definition: an effect of anticlimax created by an unintentional lapse in mood from the sublime to the trivial or ridiculous
senses.example: The ode slides into bathos when the poet rhymes "glory" with "gory."

senses.definition: (of a young person) inexperienced and immature
senses.example: He was a callow youth of seventeen when he enlisted.

senses.definition: bad-tempered or irritable
senses.example: The choleric old man shouted at the children.

senses.definition: to disparage someone or something
senses.example: He never missed a chance to derogate his rivals.

senses.definition: to detract from something
senses.example: The flaws do not derogate from the book's achievement.

senses.definition: a lament for the dead, especially one forming part of a funeral rite
senses.example: The band played a dirge as the coffin passed.

senses.definition: to make someone feel uneasy or embarrassed
senses.example: The question discomfited the minister.

senses.definition: digressing from subject to subject
senses.example: The memoir is discursive but charming.

senses.definition: shining brightly; radiant
senses.example: The effulgent sunrise lit up the whole valley.

senses.definition: to cause someone to feel drained of energy or vitality; to weaken
senses.example: The long, humid summer enervated everyone.

words.note: Enervate means to weaken, the opposite of what it sounds like.

senses.definition: a person who takes particular pleasure in fine food and drink
senses.example: An epicure, he traveled across France to sample its cheeses.

senses.definition: (of a person) not easily disturbed or angered; calm and even-tempered
senses.example: Her equable temperament made her an ideal nurse.

senses.definition: (of a climate) not varying greatly
senses.example: The island has an equable climate.

senses.definition: very small in size or amount
senses.example: They lived on an exiguous income.

senses.definition: to manipulate the boundaries of an electoral constituency so as to favor one party or class
senses.example: The ruling party gerrymandered the districts before the vote.

senses.definition: used to refer to something very light, thin and insubstantial or delicate
senses.example: The bride wore a gossamer veil.

senses.definition: a fine, filmy substance consisting of cobwebs spun by small spiders
senses.example: Gossamer glistened on the dewy grass.

senses.definition: to complain pettily; to grumble
senses.example: The players groused about the early practice.

senses.definition: a complaint or grumble
senses.example: His main grouse was the lack of parking.

senses.definition: a biography that idealizes its subject
senses.example: The authorized biography was little more than hagiography.

senses.definition: unwilling or unable to change because of tradition or convention
senses.example: The hidebound committee rejected every new idea.

senses.definition: not feeling or showing emotion
senses.example: The judge remained impassive as the verdict was read.

senses.definition: a spoken curse
senses.example: He muttered imprecations against the referee.

senses.definition: (of an action or situation) likely to arouse or incur resentment or anger in others
senses.example: Picking one winner from so many good entries was an invidious task.

senses.definition: (of a comparison or distinction) unfairly discriminating; unjust
senses.example: It would be invidious to single out one volunteer for praise.

senses.definition: a strict disciplinarian, especially in the armed forces
senses.example: The new sergeant was a martinet who punished the slightest lapse.

senses.definition: apparently attractive but having in reality no value or integrity
senses.example: The ad was full of meretricious promises.

senses.definition: larger or more generous than is usual or necessary
senses.example: A munificent gift from a former pupil saved the school.

senses.definition: strong public criticism or verbal abuse
senses.example: The ministers faced obloquy for the failed policy.

senses.definition: disgrace, especially that brought about by public criticism
senses.example: The scandal brought him years of obloquy.

senses.definition: noisy and difficult to control
senses.example: The obstreperous crowd shouted down the speaker.

senses.definition: a song of praise or triumph
senses.example: The novel is a paean to the city of Lisbon.

senses.definition: an artistic work in a style that imitates that of another work, artist or period
senses.example: The opera is a pastiche of eighteenth-century styles.

senses.definition: lacking inspiration or excitement; dull
senses.example: The novel's plot is pedestrian and predictable.

words.note: As an adjective, pedestrian means dull and ordinary.

senses.definition: translucently clear
senses.example: The pellucid stream showed every stone on its bed.

senses.definition: easily understood
senses.example: Her pellucid explanation helped everyone follow the theory.

senses.definition: the quality of having strong moral principles; honesty and decency
senses.example: No one doubted the judge's probity.

senses.definition: a tendency to choose or do something regularly; an inclination or predisposition toward a particular thing
senses.example: He has a proclivity for exaggeration.

senses.definition: to win or regain the favor of a god, spirit or person by doing something that pleases them
senses.example: The villagers made offerings to propitiate the gods.

words.note: Propitiate means to appease; propitious means favorable.

senses.definition: having or encouraging an excessive interest in sexual matters
senses.example: The tabloid fed its readers' prurient curiosity.

senses.definition: to make a forcefully reproachful protest
senses.example: He remonstrated with the referee over the penalty.

senses.definition: the use of clever but false arguments, especially with the intention of deceiving
senses.example: The lawyer's argument was pure sophistry.

senses.definition: superficially plausible, but actually wrong
senses.example: The report rests on a specious argument.

senses.definition: an excessive amount of something
senses.example: A surfeit of rich food left him ill.

senses.definition: a book, especially a large, heavy, scholarly one
senses.example: He carried a dusty tome on Roman law.

senses.definition: to deprive of freedom of action
senses.example: The artist felt trammeled by the gallery's demands.

senses.definition: a restriction or impediment to someone's freedom of action
senses.example: She escaped the trammels of small-town life.

senses.definition: excessively or ingratiatingly flattering; oily
senses.example: The unctuous salesman called everyone "my friend."

senses.definition: (of countryside) green with grass or other rich vegetation
senses.example: The verdant hills rolled down to the sea.

senses.definition: (of a person) young and inexperienced
senses.example: Verdant recruits made up half the regiment.

senses.definition: to spoil or impair the quality or efficiency of
senses.example: A single error vitiated the whole experiment.

senses.definition: to destroy or impair the legal validity of
senses.example: Fraud vitiates any contract.

senses.definition: to blame or insult someone in strong or violent language
senses.example: The coach vituperated the referee after the game.

senses.definition: speaking or spoken incessantly and fluently
senses.example: The voluble tour guide never stopped talking.

senses.definition: dislike of or prejudice against people from other countries
senses.example: The campaign played on xenophobia.
